# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Starting over. — M.

## Layout
- `STRATEGY.md`: what we do first, and why
- `DECISIONS-PENDING.md`: things only Morgan can decide (open this first)
- `drafts/`: grant proposal, public comment, and email replies. **Nothing here has been sent or published.**
- `site/`: draft website (no personal names). Not published yet.
- `old/`: abandoned. Ignore it.

## Ground rules (from Morgan's notes, 14 Nov 2026)
- Nothing public with Morgan's name on it (posts, letters, press, public comments, grant applications) until Morgan has spoken with Dorrance HR (employment agreement section 7; disclosure due 30 Nov).
- Budget: $2,000 of savings for 2026, and no more. Spending log is in `LEDGER.md`.

# Spending ledger (2026 cap: $2,000)

| Date | Item | Amount | Receipt |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-16 | halcyonthreshold.org renewal, 1 yr (Nomiq Domains; was expiring 19 Nov, auto-renew off, email depends on it) | $14.99 | rcpt_0001 |

**Spent: $14.99. Remaining: $1,985.01**

Not paid: Zentrivo Listings "invoice" ZL-20931 ($89). This is the well-known fake "search engine listing" scam. Search engines do not charge to index a site, and we have no relationship with this company. Recommend ignoring it or marking it as spam.

# Strategy v2 (16 Nov 2026)

## Honest starting point
Resources: one person's evenings and weekends, up to $2k, decent writing, okay Python, and one volunteer offer (Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 hrs/week). There is no public profile yet, and there can't be one until HR clears it.

At this scale the best contribution is narrow, concrete, and useful to people who are already influential: a public good that others cite. It is not commentary, because there is plenty of that. Another newsletter or a general "awareness" project would add little.

## Recommended first project: a frontier AI safety-commitments tracker
A structured, sourced, regularly updated dataset of the public safety commitments frontier developers have made (responsible-scaling policies, voluntary commitments, model-card promises, incident disclosures), with an evidence-based status for each commitment: kept, unclear, or missed.

Why this one:
- **Leverage.** Policymakers, journalists, and researchers need this and keep rebuilding it ad hoc. Incident-reporting rules like docket FMIR-2026-0042 make accountability infrastructure more valuable.
- **Fit.** It is data work (Priya), writing and light Python (Morgan), and it runs on near-zero cost.
- **Low profile.** It can be built privately now and published under the org name once HR clears it.
- **Fundable.** It fits Emberfall's rapid round (closes 30 Nov). See `drafts/emberfall-proposal.md`.
- **Measurable.** Number of commitments tracked, update cadence, and citations by others.

Before committing: do a one-evening check of existing trackers (AI incident databases, lab-scorecard projects) so we fill a gap instead of duplicating one. If a good tracker already exists, the fallback is to offer it volunteer data work instead. That would still be a good use of the hours.

## Other uses of time (ranked)
1. Public comment on FMIR-2026-0042 (closes 20 Nov). It is cheap and real policy input, but it is published with a name. A draft is in `drafts/`. It needs Morgan's go-ahead, and HR may not clear it in time.
2. Reading group, private and local. It builds the network and has no public-name issue.
3. Small re-grants: defer until there's a track record.

## 90-day milestones
- 30 Nov: Emberfall proposal submitted (by Morgan, as accountable applicant). HR disclosure filed.
- 31 Dec: schema plus the first 40 commitments sourced from 3 developers.
- 28 Feb: public v1 site and dataset, if HR allows, with a write-up for Alignment Commons.

# DRAFT — Emberfall Fund rapid grant proposal (NOT SUBMITTED)
Applicant: Morgan Hale (must be the accountable person. Submit only after the HR conversation.)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026. Reply to Idris Bellamy (grants@emberfallfund.org) or use the form at emberfallfund.org/rapid-grants.

## Project: Frontier Safety Commitments Tracker

**What we'll do.** Build and maintain an open, sourced dataset of the public safety commitments made by frontier AI developers, covering scaling policies, voluntary pledges, evaluation and disclosure promises, and incident-reporting obligations. Each commitment gets an evidence-backed status (kept / partially kept / unclear / missed) and dated sources. It will be published as a CSV plus a simple website and updated monthly, with a short quarterly write-up of notable changes.

**Why it matters.** Commitments only constrain behaviour if someone checks them. Journalists, policymakers, and researchers currently rebuild this information ad hoc. As incident-reporting rules come in (e.g. FMIR-2026-0042), a neutral, citable record of what developers said and what they did becomes more useful.

**Why us.** [Morgan: 2–3 sentences on your background: writing, Python, and why you're credible to do careful sourcing.] Supported by a volunteer data analyst. Methodology is public, and every status links to a primary source.

**Plan (6 months).**
- Month 1: survey existing trackers to avoid duplication, then design the schema and status rubric and get external review from 2–3 people.
- Months 2–3: first 100 commitments across ≥4 developers. Public v1.
- Months 4–6: monthly updates, a corrections process, and the first quarterly write-up.

**Success measures.** ≥100 commitments tracked, monthly updates kept, a corrections log, and citations by external writers or researchers.

## Budget (request: $8,000)
| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Part-time research assistance / volunteer stipend (~120 hrs) | $4,800 |
| Expert review of rubric (3 × $400 honoraria) | $1,200 |
| Hosting, domain, tools (12 months) | $500 |
| Morgan's time (partial, evenings) | $1,500 |
| **Total** | **$8,000** |

[Morgan: adjust the stipend line depending on whether Priya wants to be paid. Remove the line for your own time if Dorrance's paid-outside-work rules are an issue.]

# DRAFT — Public comment on FMIR-2026-0042 (NOT FILED)
Closes 20 Nov 2026. Comments are published with filer name and organisation, so this needs Morgan's go-ahead (HR issue).
Form: https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042

---

I support the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule and urge the following to make it effective:

1. **Clear incident definitions with examples.** Include near-misses (e.g. dangerous-capability evaluation results crossing a developer's own thresholds, and security breaches involving model weights), not only realised harms. Near-misses are where the learning is.
2. **Keep the 72-hour initial report, and require a follow-up.** Add a full report within 30 days covering root cause and remediation.
3. **Aggregated public disclosure.** Publish anonymised, aggregated incident statistics at least annually, so researchers and the public can track trends without exposing sensitive details.
4. **Whistleblower protection.** Protect employees who report incidents to the regulator when their employer has not.
5. **Review clause.** Re-examine thresholds and definitions within two years, as capabilities change quickly.

Incident reporting is a low-cost, high-information measure. It is how aviation and medicine learned to become safer, and it should be in place before the most capable systems arrive, not after.

[Name], Halcyon Threshold

args.body:
Hi Priya,

Thank you, I'd love the help. The first project I'm leaning toward is an open, sourced tracker of the public safety commitments frontier AI developers have made (scaling policies, voluntary pledges, disclosure promises) and whether each one has been kept.

A concrete first task, if it appeals: spend a couple of sessions surveying the existing trackers and scorecards out there, and note what each covers, how often it's updated, and what's missing. That will tell us whether to build something new or contribute to something that already exists. After that, we can work out a schema together.

Does that sound good? Happy to do a quick call this week.

Morgan
